bug_semantics: tcpliveplay accepts a user-supplied pcap, obtains each packet from libpcap, rewrites its headers, and recalculates checksums. fix_all_checksum_liveplay derives the TCP checksum length solely from the untrusted IPv4 total-length/header-length fields as ntohs(iphdr->ip_len) - (iphdr->ip_hl << 2), without bounding that result by the pcap record's caplen. do_checksum_liveplay passes this length to do_checksum_math_liveplay, whose 16-bit loop reads that many bytes from the TCP-header pointer. A crafted pcap can therefore make the loop read beyond libpcap's heap packet buffer, causing the reported heap-buffer-overflow and denial of service.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable checksum-length trust and unbounded checksum loop entered tcpreplay together when the externally developed tcpliveplay source was first imported as a new file in commit 0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01. Later commits e5039a91fbf018b5c7d084224c884e2275529724 (function rename) and 8f3761d212d39d82a3f2cad39f9f92c1ebc3ca5c (cleanup/formatting) preserved the same flaw and are not introducers.

evidence: Advisory source https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-6CVX-MW62-87PQ identifies CVE-2025-51005/GHSA-6cvx-mw62-87pq, tcpliveplay 4.5.1, crafted-pcap processing, do_checksum_math_liveplay in tcpliveplay.c, heap-buffer-overflow, and denial of service; it provides no patched-version record (`vulnerabilities` is empty).

First-party issue https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/925 gives the ASan reproduction on 4.5.1: rewrite -> fix_all_checksum_liveplay -> do_checksum_liveplay -> do_checksum_math_liveplay, a READ of size 2 exactly past a 2048-byte libpcap heap allocation. The reporter explicitly notes that `ntohs(iphdr->ip_len) - (iphdr->ip_hl << 2)` can be large. The issue is labeled `shelved` (`Will not be addressed in foreseeable future`); maintainer comments on 2025-07-12 say no more tcpliveplay updates and close it without a code fix.

At tag v4.5.1 (peeled commit 0ba7d17fcb9ddedf61168f99c249b30731310d4e), src/tcpliveplay.c calls `do_checksum_liveplay(..., ntohs(iphdr->ip_len) - (iphdr->ip_hl << 2))`, then calls `do_checksum_math_liveplay((u_int16_t *)tcp, len)`; the latter loops `while (len > 1) { sum += *data++; len -= 2; }`. src/common/utils.c:217-258 validates pcap record len/caplen relationships but does not validate IPv4 ip_len against caplen.

`git log v4.5.1 -L 1084,1086:src/tcpliveplay.c` traces the vulnerable length expression through formatting commit 8f3761d212d39d82a3f2cad39f9f92c1ebc3ca5c and rename commit e5039a91fbf018b5c7d084224c884e2275529724 to 0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01, where the file is added from /dev/null with the same expression (then calling do_checksum_newconn). `git log --all -S 'ntohs(iphdr->ip_len) - (iphdr->ip_hl << 2)' -- src/tcpliveplay.c` independently returns only 0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01.

`git rev-parse 0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01^` returns e7f6ea96f6531bb71b68b206140ef033ff16f5fa. `git ls-tree -r --name-only e7f6ea96f6531bb71b68b206140ef033ff16f5fa -- src/tcpliveplay.c` returns no entry, while commit 0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01 adds the entire 1303-line file; this directly verifies parent absence.

`git for-each-ref --contains=0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01 --sort=creatordate refs/tags` shows the first containing prerelease as v4.0.0beta1 (peeled commit 4adacbdd9abc690e081d97e602d4460098327e97) and first stable release as v4.0.0 (peeled commit 5be5a90cfe1746747e9052386f9d410e6915d606), continuing through v4.5.1 and v4.6.1.

No closing fix exists in the validated history. `git log --all -G 'ip_len|caplen' -- src/tcpliveplay.c` finds no commit that bounds the checksum length to caplen. Commit e516e93a176d9b9e170e19c96b01be4e5b29e9fe adds only minimum Ethernet/IP/TCP-header caplen checks for a different advisory and leaves the vulnerable ip_len-derived checksum call unchanged. At master c3f6049a1de91e7d3b81543d0ecb01e465b05214, src/tcpliveplay.c still contains the unbounded call and loop; `git log -1 -S 'ntohs(iphdr->ip_len) - (iphdr->ip_hl << 2)' v4.6.1 -- src/tcpliveplay.c` likewise traces the still-present expression back to the BIC. Thus there is no fix commit or fixed-version boundary to record as of v4.6.1/current master.
reasoning: The vulnerability is caused by trusting an internal IP length rather than the actual captured-buffer extent. The smallest repository commit that first places both the unsafe length derivation and consuming checksum loop into tcpreplay is the one-parent new-file import 0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01; its direct parent has no tcpliveplay.c. The later function rename and cleanup merely preserve the same semantics, so neither is the BIC. The import is a single historical source snapshot, not a reconstructable squash aggregate in this repository. AI classification is based only on the BIC commit object: it has ordinary human author/committer identity and no AI/bot trailer or marker, yielding NOT_AI. The advisory's tested/reported release is 4.5.1, but repository ancestry places the vulnerable source in releases from v4.0.0beta1 onward. The maintainer shelved the report rather than fixing it, and both v4.6.1 and current master retain the exact vulnerable data flow, so fix SHAs are justified nulls and the case is explicitly unpatched.
